This is all normal. Friendly browser error pages are not a good way to troubleshoot and investigate. Checking the SOA records for the domain is where you start, this returns the authoritative records for the domain, including the name servers, which are the ones that actually resolve the address.

The TTL for the SOA is currently 24 hours, this means that if you change any of these records, it will not start reflecting on the internet for 24 hours. This level of caching is required for the internet to function smoothly. Normally if you are planning to change the SOA or NS records you would first set the TTL to something low, so when you make the change it is reflected quickly. You wouldn't do this BTW, but even if you wanted do, it does not look like they are. The TTL for the NS records themselves is currently 1 week, again nothing changing here.

The A record for the subdomain www is currently also set to a week long TTL. The IP that the record points to is 185.193.36.131, doing a whois on this IP shows that it is owned by Hydra Communications, a UK hosting company.

The actual response on that IP is a login page for nginx, the very thing that would normally be serving you the website. This is all normal when you do something like this, the domain and subdomain records are unlikely to change if the site is going to be up in the next week, when they are ready to launch the nginx module will just start hosting the page instead asking for a login.
